What is the following text, and where does it come from?

<text>
The 2024 Conservative manifesto sets out a “secure future” plan built on five pillars: a stronger economy, opportunities for young people, secure borders and defence, stronger communities and public services, and a pragmatic path to net zero.

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027 and abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by the end of the Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates.
- “Triple Lock Plus” so both the State Pension and pensioner tax‑free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%.
- 30 hours’ free childcare from 9 months to school start; reform Child Benefit to a household test with tapering between £120k–£160k.
- Keep to fiscal rules; reduce debt; expand export and trade deals; maintain corporation tax; extend “full expensing” to leasing when affordable.
- 10‑point SME plan (rates support, VAT threshold smoothing, prompt payment enforcement, access to finance, retained growth incentives).
- £36bn redirected from HS2 phase 2 into local transport; nationwide gigabit and standalone 5G; planning and judicial review reforms to speed infrastructure.

Innovation, regulation and government reform
- Public R&D to £22bn; AI compute investment; Advanced Manufacturing Plan; support auto, aerospace, life sciences.
- Regulatory reform using Brexit freedoms; halve spend on consultants; return civil service to pre‑pandemic size; expand digital/AI capability.

Welfare, families and education
- Reform disability benefits and assessments; tighten work capability rules; overhaul fit notes; tougher sanctions; fraud bill; complete Universal Credit rollout.
- Family Hubs in every local authority; expand childcare and wraparound care.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (competitive paid military/cyber year or civic service one weekend a month).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑value degree courses; create the Advanced British Standard; ban mobiles in school; strengthen parental rights on RSHE; expand SEND places.

Health and social care
- NHS funding rises above inflation; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech plan (NHS App as front door, AI diagnostics, data platform); dental recovery plan with NHS service requirement for new dentists; women’s health strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; implement Cass Review.

Borders, immigration and defence
- Monthly Rwanda removals to deter illegal migration; rewrite asylum treaties; legal annual cap on work/family migration that falls each year; higher visa fees and health checks.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; accelerate innovation; sustained support for Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and guarantees.

Crime and justice
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; facial recognition; tougher sentences (including whole‑life terms for more heinous murders), domestic abuse measures; build four new prisons; increase removals of foreign offenders.

Energy, net zero and environment
- Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants as backup; treble offshore wind; two SMR fleets approved within 100 days; CCS clusters; Wylfa project; keep bills down (no new green levies, no road pricing or frequent flyer levy); national energy‑efficiency vouchers.
- Protect best agricultural land from solar; no fracking; reform water sector oversight; expand nature access and tree/peat programmes; moratorium on deep‑sea mining.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes; fast‑track brownfield; lift London densities; urban development corporations; permanent FTB Stamp Duty relief; new Help to Buy; renters’ reform (end Section 21 after court changes); complete leasehold reform; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- Levelling up funds, towns endowments and community ownership; Backing Drivers Bill (ban local road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, referendums on 20mph/LTNs); £2 bus fare extended for the Parliament; rail reform via Great British Railways.

Society, culture and the Union
- Clarify in law that sex means biological sex in the Equality Act; single‑sex spaces protected; school guidance on gender.
- Support creative industries and grassroots sport; review night‑time economy; protect free speech.
- Strengthen the Union, internal market and direct UK investment across Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; implement Windsor Framework and legacy arrangements.
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
